- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.75), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overpredicts after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply lag correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecasts are above 70.00, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until price stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if sentiment turns bullish in last 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.8, -0.6, +0.9), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
